extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in algebraic geometry (readers of Vakil's 'The Rising Sea')
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition and proofs of various forms of Serre duality (vector bundles, Hom, Ext), the notion of a dualizing sheaf and trace map, and related tools (Ext, π!_sh, adjunction) for projective k-schemes, with attention to Cohen–Macaulay hypotheses and the canonical bundle identification in the smooth case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desideratum: determinant of the cotangent bundle is dualizing for smooth varieties (30.1.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is smooth, we will want ω_X = K_X in this case (recall K_X = det Ω_X) — the miracle that the canonical bundle is Serre-dualizing; in particular ω_X is an invertible sheaf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is harder to prove than the basic duality statements in the chapter; it will be proved later (Exercise 30.4.I). One can also show ω_X is invertible if X is a regular embedding in a smooth variety (Exercise 30.4.H).

rubrics_metrics.name: Desideratum: Serre duality for vector bundles (functorial and trace versions) (30.1.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For F locally free on an n-dimensional projective k-scheme X, there should be a functorial isomorphism Hi(X,F) ≅ H^{n-i}(X, F^∨ ⊗ ω_X)^∨ (equivalently a particular perfect pairing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is also a trace version: a cup product Hi(X,F) × H^{n-i}(X, F^∨ ⊗ ω_X) → H^n(X, ω_X) followed by a trace map t: H^n(X, ω_X) → k yields the pairing. The trace version (hence functorial) holds when X is Cohen–Macaulay (in particular when X is smooth). The isomorphism should be functorial in F and give a natural transformation of covariant functors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desideratum: Serre duality for Hom (functorial and trace versions) (30.1.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any coherent sheaf F on a pure n-dimensional projective k-scheme X, there is a functorial isomorphism Hom(F, ω_X) ≅ H^n(X, F)^∨ (called functorial Serre duality for Hom).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace version: the canonical composition Hom(F, ω_X) × H^n(X, F) → H^n(X, ω_X) →^t k should be a perfect pairing for a chosen trace t. For Hom, the functorial version implies the trace version (Exercise 30.1.A); the trace pairing is obtained functorially from the isomorphism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: dualizing sheaf and trace (30.1.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: A coherent sheaf ω = ω_X on a projective k-scheme X of pure dimension n together with a map t: H^n(X, ω_X) → k is called dualizing if the natural map Hom(F, ω_X) × H^n(X, F) → H^n(X, ω_X) →^t k is a perfect pairing for all coherent F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When such (ω_X, t) exists we say X satisfies Serre duality (for Hom). This is the formal definition used to justify uniqueness and to state duality theorems; earlier aspirational discussion becomes this precise definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness of dualizing sheaf and trace (Proposition 30.1.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a dualizing sheaf and trace (ω_X, t) exists for X, this data is unique up to unique isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses the functorial bijection Hom(F, ω_X) ≅ Hom(F, ω'_X) for all F and the universal property argument to produce the unique isomorphism identifying ω_X and ω'_X and their traces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serre duality for Hom on projective space P^n (30.1.6–30.1.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: For P^n_k, choose ω_{P^n} = O(-n-1) and an isomorphism t: H^n(P^n, ω_{P^n}) ≅ k; then the pairing Hom(F, ω_{P^n}) × H^n(P^n, F) → k is perfect for coherent F (in particular for sums of line bundles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 30.1.B asks to verify the perfect pairing for F = O(m); Proposition 30.1.7 proves the functorial version for all coherent sheaves by resolving them by sums of line bundles and using a five-lemma-style argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desideratum: Serre duality for Ext (functorial and trace versions) (30.1.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: A stronger version: for all i we have Ext^i(–, ω_X) ≅ H^{n-i}(X, –)^∨ (functorial Serre duality for Ext).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace version should come from a cup product Ext^i(F, ω_X) × H^{n-i}(X, F) → H^n(X, ω_X) →^t k. Functorial Serre duality for Ext implies the vector-bundle case (Exercise 30.2.I). The chapter proves the functorial Ext-version under Cohen–Macaulay hypotheses for projective schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of Cohen–Macaulay hypotheses (30.1.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Cohen–Macaulay hypotheses used in various duality statements are necessary; there exist examples of non-Cohen–Macaulay projective schemes X for which no coherent dualizing sheaf ω_X exists, demonstrated by cohomology computations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete counterexample: X the union of two 2-planes in P^4 meeting at a point; Serre duality would force certain H^1 to vanish by Serre vanishing, but it does not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and basic properties of Ext and Ext sheaves (30.2 intro, 30.2.C)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any ringed space X, Ext^i_X(F, –) is the ith right derived functor of Hom_X(F, –) (global Ext); the sheaf Ext^i_X(F, –) is the corresponding right derived functor on O_X-modules (sheafified).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remarks: Mod O_X has enough injectives so these derived functors exist. Warning: it is not automatic that Ext^i(F,G) are quasi-coherent for quasi-coherent inputs (see Exercise 13.7.A); Exercise 30.2.F addresses coherence in the quasiprojective/coherent case. Use injective resolutions to derive long exact sequences for Ext.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of Ext via locally free resolutions (IMPORTANT Exercise 30.2.E)
rubrics_metrics.description: If ... → E1 → E0 → F → 0 is a locally free resolution of F, then Ext^i(F,G) ≅ H^i(Hom(E•, G)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidance: Ext can be computed affine-by-affine using finite-rank locally free (or free) resolutions of F; choose injective resolution of G to set up relevant spectral sequences. This is crucial for computations and for proving properties like coherence of Ext sheaves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vanishing and coherence of Ext sheaves under finiteness hypotheses (Exercise 30.2.F and remarks)
rubrics_metrics.description: If F and G are coherent sheaves on a quasiprojective k-scheme X (or schemes with finite-rank locally free resolutions), then Ext^i_X(F, G) is a coherent sheaf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The argument reduces to existence of finite-rank locally free resolutions on the scheme in question and local computations; use Exercise 30.2.E and standard finiteness results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long exact sequence for Ext (30.2.G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a short exact sequence 0 → F' → F → F'' → 0, there is a natural long exact sequence ... → Hom(F'',G) → Hom(F,G) → Hom(F',G) → Ext^1(F'',G) → ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct by applying Hom(–, I•) to an injective resolution I• of G and taking cohomology; this provides the usual delta-maps and exactness properties used in many arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensor and duality identities for Ext with locally free factors (30.2.H)
rubrics_metrics.description: If E is locally free, then Ext^i(F ⊗ E^∨, G) ≅ Ext^i(F, G ⊗ E) ≅ Ext^i(F, G) ⊗ E (and related isomorphisms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key fact used to relate Ext and cohomology when tensors with vector bundles are involved; prove by showing injectivity preserved under Hom with injective targets so that Hom(–,I) commutes appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification linking Ext and cohomology for locally free left argument (30.2.I)
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is locally free and ω_X any coherent sheaf, then Ext^i(F, ω_X) ≅ H^i(X, F^∨ ⊗ ω_X) (functorial in F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This shows functorial Serre duality for Ext implies the vector-bundle version of Serre duality; see Exercise 30.2.I and follow from 30.2.H and standard computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local-to-global spectral sequence for Ext (30.2.K)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a spectral sequence with E2-term H^j(X, Ext^i(F, G)) abutting to Ext^{i+j}(F, G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct via the Grothendieck composition-of-functors spectral sequence applied to Hom(F, –) = Γ(Hom(F, –)). Requires that Hom(F, I) is Γ-acyclic for injective I (Exercise 30.2.J).

rubrics_metrics.name: Yoneda (cup) product and composition of Exts (30.2.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ext groups compose: there is a graded associative composition Ext^•(A,B) × Ext^•(B,C) → Ext^•(A,C), coming from composition of maps of injective resolutions (Yoneda product); in particular there is a cup product Hi(X,F) × Ext^j(F,G) → Hi+j(X,G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct by interpreting Ext as cohomology of Hom• between injective resolutions; this product is associative and underlies the trace/cup-product constructions used in trace versions of Serre duality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction and properties of π!_sh as adjoint to π_* for affine/finite morphisms (30.3.2–30.3.B, 30.3.C)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a ring map A → B and modules M (A-module) and N (B-module), Hom_A(M, Hom_B(A,N)) ≅ Hom_B(M_B, N); this sheafifies to define, for an affine morphism π: X → Y, a functor π!_sh: QCoh_Y → QCoh_X with adjointness π_* ⊣ π!_sh. For finite (and locally Noetherian) π, π!_sh restricts to coherent sheaves and preserves injectives in certain cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this right-adjoint construction to transfer dualizing data from Y to X. Exercises 30.3.A–C guide the affine computations, sheafification, and adjointness; caution that π!_sh notation is nonstandard and is a sheaf-level analogue of Grothendieck's π! in derived categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of a finite morphism from a projective n-dimensional scheme to P^n (30.3.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a projective k-scheme of pure dimension n, there exists a finite morphism π: X → P^n (and if X is Cohen–Macaulay, π can be chosen flat).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: choose an embedding X ↪ P^N and project from a linear space L of codimension n+1 disjoint from X to get π; if k is finite use a Veronese embedding (Exercise 30.3.D). Miracle Flatness yields flatness in the Cohen–Macaulay case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer of duality along finite flat maps for vector bundles (Proposition 30.3.8 and Corollary 30.3.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is finite flat and Y satisfies functorial Serre duality for Ext with dualizing sheaf ω_Y, then X satisfies functorial Serre duality for vector bundles with dualizing sheaf π!_sh(ω_Y). In particular, functorial Serre duality for vector bundles holds for every Cohen–Macaulay equidimensional projective k-scheme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof uses adjointness of (π_*, π!_sh), projection formula, and the fact π_*O_X is locally free when π is flat; combine with the projective-space case and the finite map to reduce general projective schemes to P^n.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer of Serre duality for Hom along finite maps without flatness (Proposition 30.3.10 and Corollary 30.3.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the trace version of Serre duality for Hom holds for Y with (ω_Y, t_Y), then functorial Serre duality for Hom holds for X with dualizing sheaf π!_sh ω_Y; no flatness hypothesis on π is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the adjointness (π_*, π!_sh) and functoriality to produce the necessary commutative diagram relating Hom_X(F, π!_sh ω_Y) and H^n(X, F) to Hom_Y(π_*F, ω_Y) and H^n(Y, π_*F). Combining with Proposition 30.3.6(a) and projective-space results yields Serre duality for Hom for all equidimensional projective schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functorial Serre duality for Ext for Cohen–Macaulay projective schemes (30.3.12–30.3.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a Cohen–Macaulay projective k-scheme of pure dimension n and π: X → P^n is finite flat, then functorial Serre duality for Ext holds for X with ω_X := π!_sh(ω_{P^n}); hence functorial Serre duality for Ext holds for all equidimensional Cohen–Macaulay projective k-schemes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategy: show Ext^i_X(–, π!_sh ω_{P^n}) and H^{n-i}(X, –)^∨ are universal δ-functors and agree at i=0; verify vanishing for sufficiently negative twists using Serre vanishing and projection formula, and the five-lemma-style δ-functor argument to extend to all i.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trace version for vector bundles via Yoneda cup product (30.3.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: The trace version of Serre duality for vector bundles can be obtained by composing the Yoneda cup product Ext^i(F, ω_X) × H^{n-i}(X,F) → H^n(X, ω_X) with the trace t: H^n(X, ω_X) → k, yielding the required perfect pairing (functorial in F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chapter indicates this outline and shows the induced map is a δ-functor map that is an isomorphism by the previous universal δ-functor argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjunction formula for the dualizing sheaf for a closed embedding (Theorem 30.4.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X ↪ Y is a closed embedding of equidimensional projective k-schemes with codimension r and Y satisfies functorial Serre duality for Ext, then ω_X = π^{-1} Ext^r_Y(π_* O_X, ω_Y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 30.4.4 shows Ext^i_Y(π_* O_X, ω_Y) = 0 for i < r; Lemma 30.4.5 establishes the functorial isomorphism Hom_X(F, π^{-1}Ext^r_Y(π_* O_X, ω_Y)) ≅ Ext^r_Y(π_* F, ω_Y) which is central to identifying ω_X.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vanishing of lower Exts for closed embedding (Proposition 30.4.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the setup of a closed embedding π: X ↪ Y of pure-dimensional projective k-schemes and Y satisfying functorial Serre duality for Ext, Ext^i_Y(π_* O_X, ω_Y) = 0 for all i < r = codim(X,Y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses Serre vanishing and the local-to-global spectral sequence for Ext together with dimension support vanishing: H^j(Y, Ext^i_Y(π_* O_X, ω_Y)(m)) vanishes for large m and for N − i > n.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functorial identification used in adjunction lemma (Lemma 30.4.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: For π: X ↪ Y closed embedding of codimension r and Y satisfying functorial Serre duality for Ext, there is a functorial isomorphism Hom_X(F, π^{-1} Ext^r_Y(π_* O_X, ω_Y)) ≅ Ext^r_Y(π_* F, ω_Y) for F in Coh_X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof is obtained by choosing an injective resolution of ω_Y, applying Hom_Y(π_* F, –) and using adjointness (π_*, π!_sh) to identify complexes computing both sides; this is the technical heart of the adjunction formula.
